delegation.decision: The human did not read the diffs. On 2026-10-13 they asked for the equivalence verdicts to come from fresh agents with no context instead. 'adjudicator' stays 'human' because the frozen contract requires it and the human owns the decision; every verdict below is the panel's. The catalog sign-off is the human's own.
delegation.panel: Fresh workflow agents with no conversation context (run wf_4bf90e2a-17a). Each saw only a blind folder: the diff sheet trimmed to the equivalence definition, the operator list and the 110 mutant sections (byte-identical to the frozen sheet's sections; trimmed sheet sha256 66f07640ce5629ec02bcdd1bda100ac791871680a91ac0578a259670238b9324), and the pinned source (morph-l2/morph 3e44e795: contracts/contracts with its OpenZeppelin imports, and common/). They never saw the predictions, the prompt, the tests, the threshold or any result.
delegation.procedure: Per file group (codec libraries 31, Rollup.sol 33, batch_header.go 46): two independent judges, one reasoning from the source and one building distinguishing scenarios (it ran every Go mutant against the original). Then one adversarial refuter attacked every mutant that either judge called equivalent. The rule, fixed before the run: a mutant is equivalent iff the refuter confirms it; disagreement or doubt means not equivalent.
delegation.blindness_audit: Every tool call of the 8 panel agents was scanned for paths outside the blind folder. None was read. The only outside paths touched were the Go toolchain and module cache.
delegation.outcome: 2 equivalent (M057, M058); 108 not equivalent. M018: both judges said equivalent, but the refuter showed their premise was false (the BatchHeaderCodecTest mock compiles and is exercised by the repo's tests), so it counts as not equivalent.

M001.reason: storeBatchIndex (V0.sol:144), called at Rollup.sol:343, writes the index at header bytes 0..7 instead of 1..8. That puts idx>>56 over the version byte and leaves byte 8 as 0. Witness: after importGenesisBatch, commitBatch for batch 1 gives a header differing at bytes 7-8 (byte 0 too for version 1), so committedBatches[1] and the CommitBatch batchHash differ (simulated in work/adj-codec-witness/sim.py).

M018.reason:
Not equivalent. Both judges set aside the only other caller with a false claim. contracts/mock/BatchHeaderCodecTest.sol does compile: its struct BatchHeaderData declares `bytes32 parentBatchHash;` at line 31, so `data.parentBatchHash` at line 113 resolves. The repo also uses it: contracts/test/base/BatchHeaderCodeV0.t.sol:16 deploys `new BatchHeaderCodecTest()`, and lines 107-122 call `computeBatchHashWithData` and assert the result.

Distinguishing scenario: deploy BatchHeaderCodecTest and call `computeBatchHashWithData(data)` with the test's own data (version 0, batchIndex 1, dataHash 0x2463..fb51, blob 0x0106..4014, prev = post = 1, withdrawRoot 4, sequencerSetVerifyHash 0xf1f58308..a1b067, parentBatchHash 0x5db19913..77623c). The function takes `_batchPtr = mload(0x40)` (=0x80) on fresh memory, because the calldata struct needs no memory decoding, and passes the caller-controlled sequencerSetVerifyHash to the mutated store at line 112. In the original, header bytes 185..216 hold the hash. In the mutant, byte 185 stays 0, bytes 186..216 hold hash bytes 0..30, and byte 217 is overwritten by parentBatchHash.

I ran a Go simulation of the exact mstore sequence plus keccak256 over 249 bytes (work/ref-codec/common/m018sim/sim_test.go):
- original return value: 0xf14fe204d280f7483ae29385d880e7ba7a8a715c3450004da41cf82bfdd8415d. This matches the hash the repo test asserts, which confirms the simulation is faithful.
- mutant return value: 0xc8ff0eb190a646ce2ff96ebe338d82c1edf4225bcc24ae9e49e5338868ab207a.
So the return data differs, and the repo's own test_btach_decode1 would fail on the mutant. Any non-zero sequencerSetVerifyHash gives a difference.

Rollup and MockRollup on their own: I found no distinguishing scenario, and the judges' memory argument holds. Rollup.sol:351 stores bytes32(0). newBatchPtr is the free pointer after _commitBatch (Rollup.sol:337). The free pointer only grows (loadAndValidate bumps it by the exact length, _commitBatch reserves 10+32n bytes, the V2 blob scratch bumps after writing, and ABIv2 external calls with returns bump it by the rounded returndatasize). The only writes above the free pointer are external-call encodings and outputs of at most 36 bytes, plus the _commitBatch prelude reaching F+39 below newBatchPtr. So newBatchPtr+185 is untouched, still-zero memory in commitBatch, commitState and commitBatchWithProof; the simulation with seq=0 gives the same hash for both. Equivalence would hold only if the scope were limited to Rollup's bytecode. The sheet and task say library code is reached through its callers, and BatchHeaderCodecTest is a compiling caller with a public entry point, so the verdict is NOT equivalent.

M057.reason: I could not find a distinguishing scenario. For a uint256, `_count >= 0` is always true, so the mutant can only behave differently if the original's `_count > 0` is ever evaluated with _count==0. That would mean the loop ran all c iterations without hitting the break. It cannot. Rollup.sol:431 rejects c==0, and :439 uses checked arithmetic for b+c, so the sum cannot wrap, and it requires committedBatches[b+c]==0. Inside the loop (:444-467), the only storage writes are: zeroing committedBatches[_batchIndex] for indices b..b+c-1 (:447), batchChallengeReward and inChallenge (:450-451), `delete challenges` (:453) and revertReqIndex (:456). None of them writes a nonzero value into committedBatches. There are no external calls in the loop: batchInChallenge (:691-693) is a public view called internally, and emit makes no call. So nothing can reenter and refill committedBatches[b+c]. The unchecked increment (:460-461) cannot wrap, because _batchIndex stays at or below b+c, which is bounded. After iteration k (k=1..c), :463 reads committedBatches[b+k]. At the latest when k=c, it reads committedBatches[b+c]==0, and the break at :464-465 fires before the while condition is re-evaluated, possibly earlier. So every evaluation of the condition sees _count>=1, where both versions are true. The two versions follow the same path on every reachable state: same reverts, same events and same storage. Only gas could differ, and gas is not an observable.

M058.reason: I could not find a distinguishing scenario. The mutant's condition `revertReqIndex >= 0 && _batchIndex == revertReqIndex` reduces to `_batchIndex == revertReqIndex`. It differs from the original only when revertReqIndex==0 and _batchIndex==0. (1) This state is unreachable inside the loop. Rollup.sol:441 requires _batchIndex > lastFinalizedBatchIndex >= 0, so the first iteration has _batchIndex>=1. Each later iteration only increments it (:460), and it cannot wrap, because _batchIndex <= b+c and b+c is checked at :439. (2) Even if the state were reached, the mutant would write 0 into revertReqIndex, a uint256 at Rollup.sol:91 in its own slot, which already holds 0. Every storage slot would be unchanged. The branch emits no event and makes no call, and the return data and revert behaviour are identical. revertReqIndex is otherwise only set to batchIndex in _challengerWin (:804) and read in nonReqRevert (:132) and initialize4 (:214), so neither path is affected. Only gas could differ, and gas is not an observable.
